post.caption: A horse bridle became a necklace. The big crescent on a squash blossom necklace is called a naja, the Navajo word for crescent. It began as a crescent ornament on a horse's bridle, and the shape goes back to the Moors of North Africa. In the 1800s, Navajo men learned metalwork from Mexican smiths and made their first silver from melted coins. Each round bead is two hammered halves, soldered into a hollow globe. The first necklaces were all silver, and turquoise came later. In 2011, New Mexico made the squash blossom the official state necklace.
